items.title: Nozomi Networks and Sophos partner to integrate OT and IT security data
items.text: Nozomi Networks and Sophos have joined forces to enhance operational technology security data integration. This strategic alliance enables security teams to collaborate on investigations involving both IT and OT environments. By providing a unified view of connected systems, the partnership optimizes the correlation of security information from diverse sources, leading to accelerated threat assessment and response capabilities for organizations, strengthening their overall security posture.

items.title: Compliance spending shifts from people to platforms: Mid-year GRC trends 2026
items.text: Indian organizations are integrating governance into product design and board discussions. Data protection laws are driving execution beyond mere documentation and policy drafting. Boards now demand live risk dashboards and active oversight of technology. AI systems are creating new governance challenges requiring continuous tracking and accountability. Technology investment is replacing talent acquisition for modern compliance needs.

items.title: 10 Cybersecurity Lessons for CISOs
items.text: As India enters its 80th Independence year, digital independence is becoming as much about securing data, identity, infrastructure and AI as protecting borders. For CISOs, the next chapter demands resilience, strategic autonomy and the ability to secure innovation at scale.

items.title: Deloitte India partners with CrowdStrike to modernize cybersecurity operations in India
items.text: Deloitte India and CrowdStrike are expanding their global partnership in India. This collaboration will offer organizations access to CrowdStrike's Falcon platform. Deloitte India will provide consulting and managed security services for platform deployment. The partnership focuses on threat detection, response, and security operations. This aims to help organizations modernize security and accelerate digital transformation.

items.title: From kill switch to control: how india can protect against AI dependency
items.text: A recent AI vendor shutdown highlighted critical risks for businesses relying on external cloud models. Indian companies face growing data regulations and need to control their AI operations. The nation is developing local AI alternatives and compute resources for greater independence. Embracing open-source and hybrid solutions offers resilience and platform autonomy. This strategic shift ensures operational continuity and genuine technological independence for Indian firms.

items.title: AI to reshape banking, governance must evolve to curb cyber risk
items.text: Artificial intelligence is set to reshape India's banking sector over the next decade, but banks, regulators and the government will need to strengthen governance, cybersecurity capabilities and shared infrastructure to ensure responsible and secure adoption of the technology, said Hardik Shah, Managing Director and Partner at Boston Consulting Group (BCG).

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6-Cyber for cybersecurity teams to combat AI cyberattacks
items.text: OpenAI is set to unveil GPT-5.6-Cyber, designed specifically for cybersecurity teams striving to enhance defense mechanisms against autonomous cyberattacks. The initiative, dubbed Daybreak, introduces two distinct tiers focused on advancing defensive security research. With impressive performance in intricate tasks, GPT-5.6-Cyber is anticipated to be adopted by leading security providers, revolutionizing their cybersecurity products.

items.title: Cyber resilience will become India's next boardroom KPI
items.text: Cyber resilience has transitioned into a crucial focus for boardrooms, transcending mere operational issues. With the integration of AI and evolving data protection regulations, cybersecurity conversations are shifting. Boards should pivot from questioning their security posture to evaluating their overall resilience. This involves ingraining resilience in personnel, procedures, governance, and technology. The future of enterprise maturity and sustained business value hinges on effective cyber resilience.

items.title: OpenAI flags potential 'critical' cybersecurity capabilities in upcoming Astra model
items.text: OpenAI on Friday said its upcoming artificial intelligence model, Astra, has demonstrated significant advances in agentic coding and cybersecurity, prompting the company to conclude that it cannot currently rule out the model reaching the "Critical" cybersecurity capability threshold under its Preparedness Framework.

items.title: AI's dark side? Palo Alto Networks' NOVA system finds thousands of critical open-source vulnerabilities
items.text: Palo Alto Networks' new AI system discovered many unknown software vulnerabilities. NOVA analyzed thousands of open-source projects over two months. It identified nearly forty percent of flaws as high or critical severity. The system also found thousands of supply-chain risks within dependency packages. This AI advancement accelerates vulnerability discovery and requires rapid remediation efforts.

The lack of password salting enables offline dictionary or brute-force attacks against the password hashes.
